entries.note: Challenge basketAccessChallenge (Broken Access Control): view another user's basket. Verified at routes/basket.ts lines 18-32, which load Basket id from the route and return it after a login check that does not compare the id to the caller's basket.

Challenge basketManipulateChallenge (Broken Access Control): add a product to another user's basket. Verified at routes/basketItems.ts lines 36-49. The mismatch check uses the first BasketId and the write uses the last.

Challenge forgedReviewChallenge (Broken Access Control): edit another user's review. The project's vuln-line markers are routes/updateProductReviews.ts lines 16 and 18. The update does not constrain the author.
Challenge changeProductChallenge (Broken Access Control). The project's vuln-line is the commented-out isAuthorized middleware on PUT /api/Products/:id at server.ts line 398.
Challenge forgedFeedbackChallenge (Broken Access Control): post feedback as another user. routes/verify.ts lines 30-36 notice a mismatched UserId and still call next().
The next line, server.ts 399, denies DELETE /api/Products/:id. That is the safe look-alike beside the uncommented product PUT.
updateUserProfile loads the user with the session token's id (lines 17-25) and does not take an object id from the client. CSRF on this handler is excluded separately and is not this label.

Challenges loginAdminChallenge, loginBenderChallenge, loginJimChallenge, and ephemeralAccountantChallenge are outcomes of one SQL injection. The project's vuln-line is routes/login.ts line 34, which concatenates the email into sequelize.query. One site, not four.

Challenges unionSqlInjectionChallenge and dbSchemaChallenge share the project's vuln-line at routes/search.ts line 23. christmasSpecialChallenge is solved by ordering a product that this search injection is documented to reveal. One site.
Challenge noSqlCommandChallenge (Injection): a sleep via the reviews query. Verified at routes/showProductReviews.ts line 36, which concatenates the id into a MongoDB $where string.
Challenge noSqlOrdersChallenge (Injection). Verified at routes/trackOrder.ts line 18, which concatenates the order id into a MongoDB $where string.
Challenge noSqlReviewsChallenge (Injection). The project's vuln-lines are routes/updateProductReviews.ts lines 18 and 20: the id comes from the body and multi is true.

Challenge sstiChallenge (Injection): command execution through the profile username. Verified at routes/userProfile.ts lines 57-65, which eval a slice of the username. The username XSS challenge on the same handler is excluded.
routes/basket.ts line 19 loads the basket with a bound where clause. That query is the safe injection look-alike. The missing ownership check on the same read is the separate authz label.
The product search tool at routes/chat.ts lines 123-128 passes the term through Sequelize Op.like, which binds the value. That is a safe look-alike beside the concatenated search query.

Challenge exposedCredentialsChallenge (Sensitive Data Exposure): a testing account hardcoded on the client. Verified at frontend/src/app/login/login.component.ts lines 68-69. The literal is not repeated here.
Challenge iacLeakedKeyChallenge. The project's vuln-line is the private_key assignment at terraform/networking.tf line 171. The key material is not repeated here.
The same iacLeakedKeyChallenge marker is on infrastructure/terraform/networking.tf line 171, a second copy of the private key at this commit.
routes/chat.ts line 110 reads the LLM API key from LLM_API_KEY and defaults to empty. That is the safe look-alike beside the hardcoded testing credential and the private key.

Challenge ssrfChallenge (Broken Access Control in the project's list, SSRF in the description): the server requests a hidden resource. Verified at routes/profileImageUrlUpload.ts lines 18-24, which fetch the caller-supplied image URL with no allowlist.
lib/webhook.ts lines 14-18 fetch only when SOLUTIONS_WEBHOOK is set, and the URL is that environment variable, not request data. That is the safe SSRF look-alike.
